sources.title: Why CIPS Certification? (I.S.P. and ITCP requirements)

pathways.name: Education route (IT degree or diploma)
pathways.summary: An IT-related degree or diploma plus a minimum number of years of IT work that depends on the program. A computer science degree from outside Canada usually counts as a non-accredited university degree.

pathways.name: Experience-only route
pathways.summary: For a non-IT degree or diploma, or none: 8 years of IT professional work experience.

requirements.title: CIPS membership
requirements.description: You must be a CIPS member before you apply and attach your membership card to the application.

requirements.title: Transcripts or education equivalency assessment
requirements.description: Sent to CIPS directly by the institution or the assessment centre.

requirements.title: Years of IT professional experience
requirements.description: The minimum depends on your education. You must currently work at SFIA responsibility level 3 or higher.

requirements.title: Current IT work
requirements.description: At least 1,000 hours of IT work in the last 12 months.

requirements.title: References
requirements.description: Reference letters covering your last two years of work.

requirements.title: Résumé and SFIA skills assessment
requirements.description: Your résumé or CV and a self-assessment against the SFIA skills framework, in the experience section of the application.

requirements.title: Application and review fee
requirements.description: The CIPS certification application form, the review fee receipt and the documents above, sent to CIPS certification.

documents.name: Transcripts or equivalency assessment
documents.description: Sent directly by the institution or assessment centre.

documents.name: Reference letters for the last two years
documents.description: From people who know your recent work.

timelines.name: Recertification every three years
timelines.description: At least 100 professional development credits and evidence of active IT work (about 3,000 hours) over the three years.

open_questions: The I.S.P. is voluntary: working in computing in Alberta doesn't require it. Calling yourself a software engineer is a different matter, governed by APEGA.
The regular CIPS membership fee (needed before applying) is shown only on the membership application, not on the pages used.
CIPS Alberta's homepage says the I.S.P. is the only IT designation recognized by law in Alberta; the legislation itself has not been captured.
